mainTopic: When the men who freed a woman may marry her, and the start of the chapter on two sisters who fall to the same brothers for יבום.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a point from the previous page: a rumor alone is not enough to take a woman away from her husband. Then a משנה teaches when the men who helped free a woman to remarry may marry her themselves. They may do so if their own wives died, or if she married someone else in between. She may also always marry their sons or brothers. The גמרא first discusses whether divorcing one's own wife also lifts the ban. It answers that this depends on whether there was a quarrel, or on who started it. Next it reads the 'married someone else' case as one death and one divorce, so the משנה fits רבי's view of חזקה after two times. It then explains why his sons and brothers may marry her, and why the משנה does not bother to mention his father. Then the chapter כיצד אשת אחיו ends, and a new משנה teaches that two sisters who fall to the same brothers for יבום must do חליצה, except when an ערוה cuts the bond. The גמרא asks whether this proves that זיקה is real, suggests another reason based on not losing the מצוה of יבום, and begins a new challenge that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: No removing a wife because of a rumor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a comparison from the previous page. Just as in the other case we do not take a wife away from her husband because of a rumor alone, here too we do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of a rumor we do not remove her. Here too, because of a rumor we do not remove her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up a discussion that started on the previous page. It concludes that a rumor by itself is not enough to force a woman away from her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא compares two cases. In the earlier case it is already clear that a רננה (rumor) does not cause us to separate a married couple. The line says the same rule applies 'here too,' so this case also stays as it is. This closes the topic before the new משנה begins.

keyTerms.meaning: A rumor or gossip, without real witnesses
We remove (we take her out of the marriage)
Here too: the same rule applies to this case

steps.whatToRemember: A rumor alone is not grounds for separating a married couple.

phrases.english: Because of a rumor, we do not remove her,
phrases.notes: 'Remove her' means making her leave her husband. This finishes a comparison from the previous page.

phrases.english: here too, because of a rumor we do not remove her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an argument begun on the previous page.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A rumor alone does not cause us to separate a woman from her husband.

steps.title: If their own wives died, they may marry her
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. All the men who helped free a woman to remarry, and who were married at the time, may marry her if their own wives later died.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all of them who had wives, and their wives died, the women are permitted to marry them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says that the men from the earlier list may marry the woman they freed, if their own wives died afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה said that the שליח who brought a גט, the witness who said the husband died, and the חכם who permitted her should not marry her, because people may suspect they had their own motive. Here, each man was already married when he acted. Since his wife died only later, he clearly did not plan to marry this woman, so the suspicion disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of the משנה)
And all of them: the men listed in the earlier משנה
Permitted to be married

steps.confusionAlert: 'All of them' here means the men who freed the woman (the שליח, the witness, the חכם), not the women.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
And all of them who had wives, and the wives died,
phrases.notes: 'All of them' are the men from the earlier משנה who helped permit her to remarry.

phrases.english: the women are permitted to be married to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the man who freed her was married then, and his wife later died, he may marry the woman.

steps.title: If she married someone else in between, they may marry her
steps.stepSummary: If the woman first married another man and was then divorced or widowed, the man who freed her may now marry her.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all of these women who married others and were then divorced or widowed are permitted to marry them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case where the ban goes away. The woman married someone else first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are women who were forbidden to a certain man because people might suspect him. If she went on to marry a different man, it shows the first man did not free her for himself. So after that marriage ends in divorce or death, he may marry her.

keyTerms.meaning: To other men
They were divorced
They were widowed

phrases.english: And all of these women who were married to others,
phrases.notes: Now 'all of these' means the women who were forbidden to these men.

phrases.english: and were divorced or were widowed,
are permitted to be married to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second case where the ban is lifted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If she married another man in between and that marriage ended, the man who freed her may marry her.

steps.title: She may marry their sons or brothers
steps.stepSummary: All these women may marry the sons or brothers of the men who freed them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all of them are permitted to their sons or to their brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a third leniency. Even when the woman is forbidden to the man himself, she may marry his son or his brother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban only applies to the man who freed her, because only he could be suspected of acting for his own benefit. His son or brother did not make the ruling or give the testimony. So the suspicion does not reach them.

keyTerms.meaning: To their sons
To their brothers

steps.whatToRemember: The ban is only on the man who freed her. It ends if his wife dies or if she marries someone else in between, and it never applies to his son or brother.

phrases.english: And all of them are permitted to their sons or to their brothers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of leniencies in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The women are permitted to the sons and brothers of the men who freed them.

steps.title: Only if the wife died, not if she was divorced
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה closely. It said 'died,' so if the man's wife was only divorced, he still may not marry the woman he freed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they died, yes. If they were divorced, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes an inference from the exact word 'died' in the משנה. This inference sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה permits the man to marry her only when his wife died. The גמרא learns from this that divorce is different. If he divorced his wife and then married the woman he freed, it looks as if he planned it all along, so the suspicion returns.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Yes
No

steps.confusionAlert: The divorce here is of the man's own wife, not the woman he freed.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
If they died, yes,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the men's own wives, from the משנה's first case.

phrases.english: if they were divorced, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the first clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the wife's death lifts the ban. If she was divorced, the man still may not marry the woman he freed.

steps.title: A teaching says even divorce is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רב הלל points out a ברייתא that allows the man to marry the freed woman even if his own wife was divorced. This goes against the reading of the משנה in Step 5.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הלל said to רב אשי: But a ברייתא teaches that he may marry her even if they (the men and their wives) were divorced!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a challenge. A ברייתא seems to say the opposite of what we just learned from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 5 the גמרא learned from the word 'died' that divorce is not enough. Now a ברייתא says 'even if they were divorced,' he may marry her. The two sources seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: they were divorced

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הִלֵּל לְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Rav Hillel said to Rav Ashi:
But it is taught: Even if they were divorced!
phrases.notes: He means: even if the men's own wives were divorced, they may still marry the woman they freed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הִלֵּל לְרַב אָשֵׁי, וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference drawn in Step 5 from the word 'died.'
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that divorce of his own wife does not allow him to marry the freed woman.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly permits it even after divorce, so the משנה and the ברייתא contradict.

steps.title: It depends on whether there was a quarrel
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about a case where there was a quarrel with his wife. The ברייתא is talking about a case with no quarrel.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this (the משנה) is where there was a quarrel, and that (the ברייתא) is where there was no quarrel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying the two sources are talking about different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he was fighting with his wife when he freed the woman, we suspect he wanted her for himself, so he may not marry her. If there was no fight then, the later divorce came from some other reason, so there is nothing to suspect.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult (the start of an answer)
a quarrel or fight between husband and wife

phrases.english: This is not difficult:
This is where there was a quarrel,
phrases.notes: 'This' is our משנה, where divorce does not allow him to marry her.

phrases.english: that is where there was no quarrel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source refers to a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא both talk about the same divorce case and disagree.
steps.terutzMaskana: With a quarrel he is suspected and forbidden; without a quarrel he is permitted.

steps.title: It depends on who started the quarrel
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: in both cases there was no quarrel at the time he freed her. The difference is whether he started the later quarrel or his wife did.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: in both cases there was no quarrel at the time. Still it is not difficult: this (the משנה) is where he started the quarrel, and that (the ברייתא) is where she started it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another way to answer the same contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here both sources talk about a quarrel that came later. If he started it, we suspect he was looking for an excuse to divorce his wife and marry the freed woman. If his wife started it, there is no reason to suspect him.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you wish, say (an alternative answer)
both this and that
started, stirred up (the quarrel)

steps.whatToRemember: Divorce of his own wife only forbids him from marrying the freed woman when there is a reason to suspect him: a quarrel at the time, or (second answer) a quarrel that he himself started.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
both this and that are where there was no quarrel,
phrases.notes: No quarrel at the time he freed her; the fight came later.

phrases.english: and it is not difficult:
this is where he started it,
that is where she started it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָא וְהָא דְּלָא הֲוַאי קְטָטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second resolution to the challenge of Step 6, alongside Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases differently: by who started the quarrel.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only way to split the cases is quarrel versus no quarrel.
steps.terutzMaskana: If he started the quarrel he is forbidden; if she started it he is permitted.

steps.title: First assumption about the next line of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, about a woman who married someone else in between. It first assumes the line means death after death, and divorce after divorce.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And all of them who married others, etc.' We first think this means a death after a death, and a divorce after a divorce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new line of the משנה and states how it first understands it. This is a setup for a question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Death after death' means: her first husband's death was known from the testimony, and then her second husband also died. 'Divorce after divorce' means: her first divorce was known from the testimony, and then her second husband also divorced her.

keyTerms.meaning: it enters our mind (our first, not final, assumption)
death after death
divorce after divorce

steps.confusionAlert: 'קא סלקא דעתין' means this is only a first guess. The גמרא may change it later, so don't treat it as the final reading.

phrases.english: "And all of them who married, etc."
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from Step 3: she married someone else and was later divorced or widowed.

phrases.english: It enters our mind to say
death after death,
and divorce after divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכוּלָּן שֶׁנִּישְּׂאוּ וְכוּ׳. קָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the divorce discussion and opens analysis of the line quoted in Step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Initial assumption: the משנה means a second death after the first death, or a second divorce after the first divorce.

steps.title: Does the משנה go against רבי?
steps.stepSummary: If a woman's two husbands died, רבי holds she has a חזקה after two times and should not remarry. Since the משנה lets her remarry, it seems not to follow רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say our משנה does not follow רבי? Because if it followed רבי, he said that after two times it becomes a חזקה!
steps.whatsHappening: Building on the assumption of Step 9, the גמרא asks whether the משנה disagrees with רבי. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two of her husbands died, רבי says this pattern makes her a woman we presume is dangerous to marry. Yet the משנה lets her marry the man who freed her. So the משנה seems to follow a different view, unless the גמרא can explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: shall we say (a suggestion, often then pushed back)
after two times
a presumption based on a pattern

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the idea that a pattern repeated twice creates a חזקה. The view of רבי on this comes up in many places in ש״ס.

phrases.english: Shall we say our Mishna is not like Rabbi,
for if it is like Rabbi, did he not say:
after two times it becomes a presumption!
phrases.notes: Here this means: after two husbands died, we presume marrying her is dangerous, so she should not marry again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a problem from the 'death after death' assumption of Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's permission for a twice-widowed woman to marry the man who freed her.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי, two deaths create a חזקה that forbids her to remarry, so the משנה would contradict רבי.

steps.title: The משנה can mean one death and one divorce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on Step 10. The משנה may mean a woman who was divorced and then widowed, or widowed and then divorced. It does not have to mean two deaths, so it can still follow רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The משנה means death after divorce, or divorce after death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge from Step 10. It reads the line of the משנה in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 assumed the משנה meant two husbands who both died, which would clash with רבי's view that two times makes a חזקה. Now the גמרא says the משנה means one death and one divorce mixed together. In that case there is no repeated pattern, so even רבי would let her remarry.

keyTerms.meaning: Death (here, of a husband)
Divorce
No. Here it rejects the proof that came before.

phrases.english: No: death after divorce,
and divorce after death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 10 that the משנה does not follow רבי.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the משנה must disagree with רבי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Step 10 assumed the משנה meant two deaths. It can mean one death and one divorce, which does not create a חזקה.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה about a woman who married someone else in between is read as one death plus one divorce. That way it fits even רבי's view of חזקה after two times.

steps.title: The suspected women may marry the man's sons or brothers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. All the women whom the man may not marry because of suspicion are allowed to marry his sons or his brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all of them are permitted to their sons or to their brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה. It is setting up a question about this line in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the משנה forbade a man to marry certain women because of suspicion. This line limits that rule: it applies only to the man himself, not to his sons or brothers.

keyTerms.meaning: And all of them (all the women listed in the משנה)
Are permitted
To their sons or to their brothers (of the men who were suspected)

phrases.english: And all of them are permitted
phrases.notes: All of them means all the women the משנה listed, whom the man himself could not marry because of suspicion.

phrases.english: to their sons or to their brothers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The suspicion forbids only the man himself. His sons and brothers may marry the woman.

steps.title: Why is this different from a suspect being forbidden to the woman's relatives?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a teaching that a man suspected with a woman may not marry her mother, daughter, or sister. There the suspicion spreads to her relatives, so why does it not spread to his relatives here?
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this different from what we learned: a man suspected with a woman is forbidden to her mother, her daughter, and her sister?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the suspicion spreads to the woman's family in another teaching but does not spread to the man's family in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the other teaching, the suspect is kept away from the woman's close relatives. By that logic, the woman should also be kept away from the suspect's close relatives, such as his sons and brothers. Our משנה allows it, so the two seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? (used to point out a contradiction)
A man who is suspected (of being with a woman)
Her mother, her daughter, and her sister

phrases.english: How is this different from what we learned:
one who is suspected with a woman,
is forbidden to her mother, her daughter, and her sister.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the line of the משנה quoted in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the suspected women may marry the man's sons or brothers.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The other teaching spreads the suspicion to the woman's relatives. Our משנה does not spread it to the man's relatives. Why the difference?

steps.title: Women often stay at each other's homes, but men do not
steps.stepSummary: Women often visit and stay over at other women's homes. So the woman he was suspected with would come to the home of her mother, daughter, or sister if he married one of them. Men do not usually stay at other men's homes, so the suspect would rarely be near his son's or brother's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Women commonly go to other women's homes. Men do not commonly go to other men's homes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by pointing to how often each side would actually meet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the suspect married the woman's relative, she would often visit and stay over, and he might sin with her again. If she married his son or brother, he would not usually stay at their home, so the risk is small.

keyTerms.meaning: Women
Men
It is common
That they go (to visit)

phrases.english: Women to other women
commonly go.
phrases.notes: Women often visit and stay over at the homes of other women, especially relatives.

phrases.english: Men to other men
do not commonly go.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases by what happens in real life.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Suspicion should spread the same way to both families.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the woman's relatives create real closeness, because women visit each other often. The man's relatives do not.

steps.title: Men watch each other closely, women do not
steps.stepSummary: A second answer. If a man sins with his wife's relative, his wife is not forbidden to him, so wives are not watchful. If a man sins with another man's wife, she becomes forbidden to her husband, so husbands watch closely and keep the suspect away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or: women, whose being with a man does not make one forbidden because of the other, are not strict with each other. Men, whose being with a woman does make one forbidden because of the other, are strict with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another reason the suspicion spreads to the woman's relatives but not to the man's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the suspect married the woman's relative and sinned with her again, his wife would stay permitted to him, so she would not guard against it. If the woman married his son or brother, a sin with her would make her forbidden to her husband. So that husband would watch carefully, and the risk is small.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively (introduces a second answer)
Their lying (being together physically)
Makes forbidden
Are strict, careful, watchful
With one another

steps.whyThisMatters: Both answers explain why a suspicion leads to a rule against marriage only when there is a real chance the sin will happen again.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי: נְשֵׁי דְּלָא אָסְרָן שְׁכִיבָתָן אַהֲדָדֵי,
phrases.english: Alternatively: women, whose lying does not make them forbidden to one another,
phrases.notes: If a man sins with his wife's relative, his wife does not become forbidden to him.

phrases.english: are not strict with one another.
Men, whose lying does make them forbidden to one another,
phrases.notes: If another man sins with a man's wife, she becomes forbidden to her husband.

phrases.english: are strict with one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי: נְשֵׁי דְּלָא אָסְרָן שְׁכִיבָתָן אַהֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the same קשיא from Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases by how watchful each side is.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Suspicion should spread the same way to both families.
steps.terutzMaskana: Husbands guard closely because a sin would forbid their wives to them. Wives have less reason to guard, so only the woman's relatives are forbidden to the suspect.
steps.whatToRemember: Two reasons the suspect's sons and brothers may marry the woman: men rarely stay at each other's homes, and husbands watch closely because a sin would forbid their wives to them.

steps.title: Why not list the father too?
steps.stepSummary: If the reason is that men don't visit each other's homes, the suspect's father should also be allowed to marry the woman. Why doesn't the משנה say so?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then his father should be allowed too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the משנה, which mentions only sons and brothers. Following the reasoning from Step 14, the father should also be listed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said the suspect will rarely be near his relative's wife, because men don't stay at other men's homes. That reason fits the father just as well as the sons and brothers. So why does the משנה leave out the father?

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if your reasoning is right
His father
Also, too

phrases.english: If so, his father too?
phrases.notes: He means: the suspect's father should also be allowed to marry the woman, so why doesn't the משנה say so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reasoning from Steps 14 and 15 to ask about a relative the משנה left out.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's list of 'his sons or his brothers'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reason applies to all male relatives, the משנה should also mention the father.

steps.title: The father is obvious; the son is the real news
steps.stepSummary: The משנה uses a 'not necessary to say' style. The father is plainly allowed, because a son is ashamed before his father. The son is the real חידוש, because a father is not ashamed before his son.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is speaking in a 'no need to say' way. There is no need to say his father is allowed, because the son is ashamed in front of his father. But his son, where the father is not ashamed in front of the son, I might think is not allowed. So the משנה teaches us that he is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the father really is allowed. The משנה skipped him because he is the obvious case and only listed the case we might have doubted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Say the suspect's father marries the woman. The suspect would feel too ashamed before his father to sin with his father's wife. Now say the suspect's son marries her. The suspect is the father here and does not feel that shame, so we might think she is forbidden. The משנה tells us that even this case is allowed, and the father's case is allowed all the more.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not necessary to say. A style where the obvious case is left out and the bigger חידוש is stated
Embarrassed, ashamed
I might say, I might think
It teaches us. This introduces the חידוש

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה lists the less obvious case, the son. The father's case is even more clearly allowed.

phrases.english: It is saying 'it is not necessary':
It is not necessary to say his father,
since his son is embarrassed before him,
phrases.notes: The 'son' here is the suspect himself. He would never sin with his own father's wife.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּנוֹ, דְּלָא בְּזִיז אָבִיו מִינֵּיהּ
phrases.english: but his son, where the father is not embarrassed before him,
I might say not,
so it teaches us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the wording with the 'not necessary to say' style
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father was left out because he is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father is permitted, and the case is too obvious to list. The son is listed because it is the bigger חידוש.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing כיצד אשת אחיו
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the second chapter of יבמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter כיצד אשת אחיו.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the chapter כיצד אשת אחיו. A new chapter begins right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a short farewell to the chapter we just finished, with the hope of learning it again. It is not part of the discussion itself.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. Said when finishing a chapter
The name of the chapter just finished, taken from its opening words

phrases.english: We will return to you,
'How is the wife of his brother'

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The second chapter of יבמות is complete.

steps.title: Two sisters fall to the same brothers
steps.stepSummary: Two of four brothers were married to two sisters and died. The sisters must do חליצה, not יבום. If brothers married them anyway, they must divorce them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Four brothers. Two of them were married to two sisters, and the brothers married to the sisters died. These women do חליצה and do not do יבום. If the brothers went ahead and married them, they must send them out.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter opens with a new משנה. It describes a case where two sisters both need יבום from the same two surviving brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each widow is tied by a יבום bond (זיקה) to each surviving brother. So for each brother, every sister is the sister of a woman who is tied to him, and the רבנן forbade that. This is why the sisters do חליצה, and anyone who married one must divorce her.

keyTerms.meaning: They do חֲלִיצָה, the ceremony that releases a widow from יבום
They marry through יִבּוּם
They went ahead and married them, without asking first
They must send them out, meaning divorce them
The יבום bond between a widow and her late husband's brothers

steps.confusionAlert: The sisters are not forbidden from the Torah here. The problem comes from the זיקה, which makes each one 'the sister of the woman tied to him.' That is a rabbinic ban.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole chapter, which is about how זיקה can create problems with relatives.

phrases.english: Four brothers,
two of them were married to two sisters,
and the ones married to the sisters died,
these women do חליצה and do not do יבום.
And if they went ahead and married them,
they must send them out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַרְבָּעָה אַחִין, שְׁנַיִם מֵהֶם נְשׂוּאִים שְׁתֵּי אֲחָיוֹת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two sisters who fall to the same brothers do חליצה, not יבום. If a brother married one, he must divorce her.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר reports a dispute
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says this is a dispute: בית שמאי allow the brother to stay married, and בית הלל say he must divorce.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: בית שמאי say he may keep her, and בית הלל say they must send them out.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings רבי אליעזר's report about the case where the brothers already married the sisters. He says this was a dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion stated 'they must divorce' as a plain rule. רבי אליעזר says only בית הלל held that, while בית שמאי let the marriage stand. This is only about the case after they already married. Everyone agrees they should start with חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: He may keep her as his wife
The students of שמאי
The students of הלל

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
Beit Shammai say: he may keep her,
and Beit Hillel say: they must send them out.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a different report about the 'already married' case in Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, בית שמאי let the marriage stand and בית הלל require divorce.

steps.title: When one sister is an ערוה to one brother
steps.stepSummary: If one sister is an ערוה to one of the brothers, that brother may not marry her but may marry her sister. The other brother is still forbidden to both.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of the sisters was forbidden to one brother as an ערוה, he is forbidden to her but allowed to her sister. And the second brother is forbidden to both of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה changes the case: one of the sisters is a forbidden relative (ערוה) to one of the brothers. It explains how that changes the rule for each brother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who is an ערוה to a brother never falls to him for יבום, so she has no bond with him. Then her sister is no longer 'the sister of a woman tied to him,' and he may do יבום with her. The second brother is still tied to both sisters, so both remain forbidden to him.

keyTerms.meaning: A ban on forbidden close relatives
Allowed to marry her sister
The second (other) brother

steps.whatToRemember: An ערוה has no יבום bond with that brother. Without the bond, her sister is not forbidden to him.

phrases.english: If one of them was
forbidden to one of the brothers as an ערוה,
he is forbidden to her and allowed to her sister.
And the second brother is forbidden to both of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיְתָה אַחַת מֵהֶן אֲסוּרָה עַל הָאֶחָד אִיסּוּר עֶרְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Changes the case from Step 19, showing what happens when there is no bond between one brother and one sister.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The brother for whom one sister is an ערוה may do יבום with the other sister. The other brother is forbidden to both.

steps.title: Lighter prohibitions still require חליצה
steps.stepSummary: If one sister is forbidden to a brother only by an איסור מצוה or an איסור קדושה, the ruling is חליצה, not יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the prohibition is only an איסור מצוה or an איסור קדושה, she does חליצה and not יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues from step 21. It says that if the sister is forbidden only by a lighter prohibition, not an ערוה, she does חליצה and not יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 21, an ערוה prohibition fully removed one sister from that brother, so he could marry the other sister. A lighter prohibition does not remove the bond of יבום, so each sister stays connected to both brothers. Because of that, the two-sisters problem from step 19 comes back, and only חליצה is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'prohibition of מצוה', a lighter, rabbinic level of forbidden relative
A 'prohibition of holiness', such as the marriage restrictions of a כֹּהֵן
She does חֲלִיצָה, the ceremony that releases her from יִבּוּם
She enters into יִבּוּם, levirate marriage

steps.confusionAlert: Do not treat every prohibition like an ערוה. Only an ערוה cuts the bond of יבום. Lighter prohibitions leave the bond in place, so she still needs חליצה.

phrases.english: A prohibition of מצוה and a prohibition of holiness
she does חליצה and does not enter into יבום

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיסּוּר מִצְוָה וְאִיסּוּר קְדוּשָּׁה — חוֹלֶצֶת וְלֹא מִתְיַיבֶּמֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts lighter prohibitions with the ערוה case in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An איסור מצוה or איסור קדושה does not remove the bond of יבום, so חליצה is required instead of יבום.

steps.title: Each sister is an ערוה to a different brother
steps.stepSummary: When each sister is an ערוה to a different brother, each one is permitted to the other brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one sister was forbidden to this brother as an ערוה, and the second sister was forbidden to that brother as an ערוה, then the one forbidden to this brother is permitted to that one, and the one forbidden to that brother is permitted to this one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a 'crossed' case. Sister A is an ערוה to brother 1, and sister B is an ערוה to brother 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ערוה fully cuts the bond, so each sister is now tied to only one brother. That means no brother is bound to two sisters at once. So each brother may take the sister who is permitted to him.

keyTerms.meaning: A full Torah prohibition of a forbidden relative
Forbidden
Permitted

phrases.english: If one of them was
forbidden to this brother with an ערוה prohibition

phrases.aramaic: וְהַשְּׁנִיָּה אֲסוּרָה עַל זֶה אִיסּוּר עֶרְוָה
phrases.english: and the second was forbidden to that brother with an ערוה prohibition
the one forbidden to this brother is permitted to that brother
and the one forbidden to that brother is permitted to this brother

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיְתָה אַחַת מֵהֶן אֲסוּרָה עַל זֶה אִיסּוּר עֶרְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends step 21's single-ערוה case to a double, crossed ערוה case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When each sister is an ערוה to a different brother, each sister is permitted to the other brother.

steps.title: This is the case of 'her sister who is her יבמה'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains that the known ruling about a sister who is also a יבמה refers to this crossed ערוה case, where she may do חליצה or יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is the case they meant when they said: 'Her sister, when she is her יבמה, either does חליצה or enters into יבום.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ties the crossed case from step 23 to a well-known saying. That saying allows a sister who is also a יבמה to do either חליצה or יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally two sisters falling to the same brothers cannot do יבום, as step 19 taught. This saying seems to allow it, so the משנה explains which case it means. It means the crossed ערוה case, where each sister is bound to only one brother.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And this is what they said', which links a case to an earlier known ruling
Her sister
Her יְבָמָה, a woman who fell to the same brothers for יבום

steps.whatToRemember: An ערוה cuts the bond of יבום, but lighter prohibitions do not. Only when each sister is an ערוה to a different brother may the two sisters do יבום.

phrases.english: And this is what they said:
her sister, when she is also her יבמה,
either does חליצה or enters into יבום

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the case from step 23 as the subject of a known ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ruling 'her sister who is her יבמה may do חליצה or יבום' refers to the crossed ערוה case.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה that זיקה is real
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from step 19 that זיקה is real. Otherwise, each brother could simply do יבום with one sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Learn from this that there is זיקה. For if there were no זיקה, these two women come from two different households, so why not let this brother do יבום with one and that brother do יבום with the other?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and tries to prove a big idea from the משנה: that זיקה, the bond of יבום, is real. This sets up a discussion of whether the proof holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sisters were married to two different brothers, so if there were no bond, nothing would stop each living brother from taking one. The משנה in step 19 still forbids יבום. That suggests each sister's זיקה makes her like a wife, so her sister becomes forbidden as a wife's sister.

keyTerms.meaning: The bond of יבום that links a widow to her late husband's brothers
'There is זיקה', meaning the bond works almost like marriage
'Learn from this', which introduces an inference
'After all', which introduces an obvious fact
From two households, meaning from two different husbands

steps.confusionAlert: Do not get mixed up about what זיקה means here. It is not a full marriage. The question is whether the bond is strong enough to make her sister forbidden, the way a wife's sister is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: Whether יש זיקה is a major question across מסכת יבמות. This step uses the two-sisters case as a test of it.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Learn from this: there is a זיקה bond
phrases.notes: He's pointing back to the rule from step 19: the two sisters must do חליצה, not יבום.

phrases.english: For if there were no זיקה bond,
after all, these women come from two households
let this brother do יבום with one
and that brother do יבום with the other?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא by drawing a general principle from the משנה's ruling in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: That זיקה is real and works like marriage (יש זיקה).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling that two sisters from two different husbands must do חליצה and not יבום, even though each brother could take one sister.

steps.title: Maybe there is no זיקה, only a worry that the מצוה will be lost
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 25. It says the משנה might hold that there is no זיקה. The ruling of חליצה comes instead from the worry that the מצוה of יבום could be cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, I can tell you there is no זיקה. The reason is that the משנה holds it is forbidden to cancel the מצוה of יבום. Perhaps while one brother is doing יבום with one sister, the other brother will die, and then the מצוה of יבום will be cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof that זיקה is real. It gives a different reason why the brothers may not do יבום with the sisters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 said the only reason to ban יבום here is זיקה. This step offers a second reason: if one brother marries one sister and the other brother then dies, the second sister falls only to the married brother. She is his wife's sister, so he cannot do יבום with her, and the מצוה is lost. Because of that risk, the משנה rules חליצה even without זיקה.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually; it signals that the speaker is keeping his own position
The bond between a יבמה and the brothers of her dead husband, which makes her somewhat like a wife to them
It is forbidden to cancel the מצוה of יבום
Perhaps / maybe
The other one

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not say that זיקה is false. It only shows that the משנה does not prove זיקה, because there is another possible reason for its ruling.

phrases.english: Really, I can tell you there is no זיקה,
and the reason is that he holds
it is forbidden to cancel the מצוה of levirate marriage.
Perhaps while one brother is doing levirate marriage,
the other brother will die,
phrases.notes: Then the second sister falls only to the brother already married to her sister. She is forbidden to him as his wife's sister.

phrases.english: and he ends up cancelling the מצוה of levirate marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 25 by giving another reason for the משנה's ruling
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the משנה that זיקה is real
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling of חליצה can be explained without זיקה, by the worry that a brother might die and the מצוה of יבום would be cancelled

steps.title: Then why not teach the case with three brothers?
steps.stepSummary: If the worry is that the מצוה might be cancelled, the משנה could have used three brothers. With three brothers the problem is even clearer.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the same should be true with three brothers too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reason from step 26. If the worry is losing the מצוה, why did the משנה choose a case with four brothers?
steps.deeperAnalysis: With three brothers, two die and leave two sisters to one living brother. He can do יבום with only one of them, so the מצוה is surely lost for the other. That case seems to fit the reason better, so why did the משנה mention four?

keyTerms.meaning: If so; it introduces a challenge built on what was just said
Three (brothers)
Also / too

phrases.english: If so,
then three brothers too?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking why the משנה described four brothers when a case of three would show the same rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 26
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה's ruling comes from the worry about cancelling the מצוה of יבום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were the reason, the משנה should have taught the case of three brothers, where the מצוה is certainly lost

steps.title: The משנה teaches 'not only three, but even four'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה uses a 'not only this, but even that' style. With three brothers the rule is obvious. Four brothers teaches that we worry about death even when it is only a possibility.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are speaking in the style of 'it is not necessary.' It is not necessary to say this about three brothers, where the מצוה of יבום is surely cancelled. But with four brothers, you might think we do not worry that one of them will die. So the משנה teaches us that we do worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 27. The משנה chose the harder case on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With three brothers the loss of the מצוה is certain, so the ruling of חליצה is obvious and needs no teaching. With four brothers the loss happens only if a brother dies, so we might have ignored that risk. The משנה teaches that even this possible loss is enough to require חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not necessary to say; a 'not only this, but even that' style of teaching
Certainly
We do not worry about the possibility of death
It teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: Even if זיקה is not real, the משנה's ruling can be explained: we worry that a brother might die and the מצוה of יבום would be lost. The משנה uses four brothers to teach that even this possible risk counts.

phrases.english: We are speaking in the style of 'it is not necessary':
it is not necessary to say this about three brothers,
where the מצוה of levirate marriage is certainly cancelled.
But with four brothers,
you might say we do not worry about death,
so it teaches us that we do.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic: 'not only this, but even that'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With four brothers, we might ignore the chance that a brother will die and allow יבום
steps.terutzMaskana: Even the possible loss of the מצוה through a brother's death requires חליצה, and the case of three is obvious
steps.whyThisMatters: It keeps alive the reading that the משנה does not prove זיקה.

steps.title: Opening a new challenge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new challenge based on the idea that we worry a brother might die.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting a new challenge, and the rest of the question comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'if so' take the answer of step 28 as true: we do worry that a brother might die. The גמרא is about to show a problem that follows from this worry.

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: This means: if we worry that the remaining brother might die. The question itself continues right after this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up a new challenge to the answer of step 28
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that we worry a brother might die
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The full attack continues on the next amud, which shows where this worry leads
